newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars petrified by Fed.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars petrified by Fed.

text.p: Interest rate futures on SIMEX were inert for most of Monday's session as a holiday in Japan and caution ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting severely hampered activity.
"There's nothing to be said about any of the markets. It's unchanged in Euroyen and practically unchanged in the Eurodollars," said a trader with a European futures house.
The lead March Euroyen contract finished at 99.17 against its CME close at 99.18 on volume of a mere 2320 lots.
December Eurodollars ended at 94.05 against their IMM settlement at 94.06.
Dealers said the market had priced in a 25-basis-point increase in the federal funds rate, the benchmark for overnight loans between banks.
"If they do nothing (tomorrow), the pressure will be on them to hike by 50 basis points early next year so that they're perceived to be ahead of the inflation curve," said the trader.
He said the Fed was unlikely to tighten credit at its next meeting, just before the U.S. presidential election, which would rule out a change in interest rates until January.
"If they hold off now, they would be losing control of the economy for three months," he said. "They would then have to move strongly to get market confidence back."
The Fed last adjusted rates on January 31, when it lowered the discount and fed funds rates by 25 basis points each.
Japanese government bond futures were not traded due to the holiday in Japan.
